clue.text: Part of revised item ready for publication

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Once an item has been revised, at least some of it is fit to print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is a verb here, not an adjective: to prepare text for printing.
explanation.definitionFit: Preparing copy for the press by correcting and cutting it is a synonym, with ready used as a verb.

clue.text: Coins mediaeval groups needed, including sovereign

indicators.note: including means the groups word holds the monarch's letters within it

parts.note: guilds were associations of craftsmen or merchants in the Middle Ages
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the reigning monarch

explanation.surface: Medieval trade associations needed money, even a gold sovereign among their funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign' looks like another coin beside 'Coins', but it is ER, the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the currency units of the Netherlands before the euro, so they are coins.

clue.text: Jerk grabbing husband is violent criminal

indicators.note: grabbing means the pulling word takes hold of the husband letter inside it

parts.note: to jerk something is to give it a sharp pull, a tug

explanation.surface: Some idiot seizing a married man turns out to be a brutal offender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' reads as an insult for a person; here it is a verb meaning pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruffian who uses violence, typically in robbery or assault, is the plain synonym.

clue.text: Old lady less polite about a roving thief

parts.note: old lady is slang for one's mother, MA

indicators.note: about means the ruder word goes round the letter a

parts.note: less polite is ruder

explanation.surface: A rude old woman is spoken of as a wandering crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider who roams looking for plunder is exactly a thief on the move.

clue.text: Fortune heirs dissipated over century

indicators.note: over means covering, so the scattered letters lie all round the century letter
dissipated means scattered, so the letters of heirs are rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: Heirs squandered the family fortune over a hundred years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts RIHES (the anagram of HEIRS, from 'dissipated') around C, the century, giving RI-C-HES.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune is a great deal of money or wealth, just as riches are.

clue.text: Living in 14

definitions.meaning: a living is the income one earns to get by, one's livelihood
put in the terms of 14 (paper money): a newspaper that comes out every day plus a slang word for money

explanation.walkthrough: 14 is PAPER MONEY: a daily is a paper and bread is slang for money, so this phrase is 14 restated.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning one's keep is a common idiom built on the Lord's Prayer phrase for basic sustenance.

clue.text: Test's first relocated over Italian island

indicators.note: first relocated means the opening letter of the test word is shifted to its end

parts.note: a test is a trial
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A cricket Test match's opening day was moved, after an over, to an island in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first relocated' moves the T of TRIAL to the back, making RIALT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a central island of Venice, home to the famous bridge and market.

clue.text: Start off nervous in this fast-paced kind of racing

indicators.note: Start off means the first letter of the nervous word is removed

parts.note: windy is British slang for scared or nervous

explanation.surface: A jittery driver gets going in a high-speed motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: WINDY, British slang for frightened, loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for Indianapolis, it names American open-wheel motor racing, as at the Indianapolis 500.

clue.text: Sticky stuff for baker or cook that's disgusting!

parts.note: to do food is to cook it, as in doing the vegetables
ugh is the exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at the gooey mixture a baker uses: cook it, or it's revolting!
explanation.definitionFit: A baker kneads a soft paste of flour and water before shaping bread or pastry.

clue.text: Vigour shown as Brendan's getting in a state

indicators.note: getting in means the setter's letters enter the a-plus-state string

parts.note: a state is a nation
Brendan is the setter, so Brendan's is I'm, the setter's own I am

explanation.surface: The setter shows energy while getting himself worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Brendan is the setter, so 'Brendan's' gives I'M; 'in a state' reads as agitated but is A NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Liveliness and spirited energy are what this word means when said of a person's manner.

clue.text: Signal that could be great help

indicators.note: could be says these letters may become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A message that might come in very handy.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to signal or send a message by wire, or to give away one's intentions.

clue.text: Stick with sweet lines about love and end of hostility

indicators.note: about means the line letters go round the love letter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, and the plural here is taken as three of them
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of hostility

explanation.surface: Someone sticks to sugary verses about love and an end to fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' here gives three Ls, not the usual two, with O placed after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop or ice on a stick, sucked as a sweet; it is also British slang for money.

clue.text: Dealt with offensive language from PM once back in base

indicators.note: in means the reversed name sits inside the base word

parts.note: a bed is a base, as the bed of a river or a flower bed

indicators.note: back means the former prime minister's name is read backwards

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a nineteenth-century British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A former prime minister's swearing, from back at his base, was censored.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Peel was a 19th-century British Prime Minister; 'back' signals the reversal, and the base is a bed, not a military one.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters cover swear words with a tone, which is exactly how they censor bad language.

clue.text: Runs into singer or section of 30

indicators.note: into means the runs letter goes inside the singer word

parts.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest voice
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into a vocalist or a part of the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 30 is ORCHESTRA; the trumpets and trombones form one of its sections.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumpets, horns and trombones together make up one family of instruments in a symphony band.

clue.text: 6 notes

definitions.meaning: 6 is DAILY BREAD; a daily is a newspaper and bread is slang for money, so the pair restated in plain words
banknotes, currency printed rather than minted

explanation.walkthrough: The two linked clues define each other: DAILY means paper and BREAD means money.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are currency printed on sheets rather than struck as coins.

clue.text: Fuel for warships in part of earth that's covered

parts.note: subs, submarines, are warships
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Fuel for naval vessels is found in buried ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The layer beneath the topsoil is earth hidden under the surface.

clue.text: Awful clue about Republican's sordid gain

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the Republican letter
awful means the word clue is in a bad state, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A terrible tip-off lets a Republican profit dishonestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts LUCE (the anagram of CLUE, from 'Awful') around R.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical phrase 'filthy' money, it means money gained in a shameful or greedy way.

clue.text: Storyteller backed main event in theatre

indicators.note: backed means the main's word is reversed

parts.note: the main is the open sea
an op, an operation, is what happens in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: A playwright supported the headline show at the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns SEA to AES; the theatre is the hospital kind, not a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek author of the fables is the classic teller of moral tales.

clue.text: Publication that raises funds for charity

definitions.meaning: a scruffy newspaper or tabloid, called disparagingly a low-quality paper
British students hold an annual charity week of stunts and collections

explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a rag week is a student fundraising festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a tabloid newspaper, and also the name of student charity fundraising events.

clue.text: Venetian who painted over an angel?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the painter's name above the next letters

parts.note: Francesco Guardi was an eighteenth-century Venetian painter of city views

explanation.surface: Which Venetian artist painted over an angel in his picture?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: protectors are called angels.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian angel watches over a person, so a protecting spirit is an example.

clue.text: Changed the current key for code

indicators.note: Changed means the letters of the word that are rearranged

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone altered the present major key used for a cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changed' shuffles THE to ETH.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral principle or set of rules for conduct is a code of behaviour.

clue.text: Fair and square in natural setting

indicators.note: in means the and-plus-square letters go inside the habitat word

parts.note: an animal's home is its natural setting or habitat
taken as written
S, a short form for square, as in street names

explanation.surface: Being honest in one's own surroundings, as in fair and square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair and square' looks like the idiom for honest; split it, and 'Fair' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair as in good-looking, or a fair sum, both match this word for attractive or generous.

clue.text: Bird in spring seen by river bank

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
a bank is a row or tier, as in a bank of seats

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted in springtime by a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' is the watery kind, and 'river bank' splits into R and ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: The common small brown songbird of gardens is a familiar example of a bird.

clue.text: One coin for each person

parts.note: a means one
a piece is a coin, as in a fifty-pence piece

explanation.surface: Each person gets a single coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means each, to or for every individual one.

clue.text: Possible result of breaking the law

definitions.text: Possible result of breaking the law

indicators.note: breaking means the words the law are smashed and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Crime may make you rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: crime can make you rich, and breaking up the letters gives the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Riches are a plausible outcome of crime, the whole clue painting the money as ill-gotten.

clue.text: A poet penning new work performed rather slowly

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so a-plus-poet holds the new letter

parts.note: Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A poet writes a new piece that is played at a leisurely pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A movement marked at a moderately slow walking pace takes its name from that tempo marking.

clue.text: First half of the big game

definitions.text: First half of the big game

parts.words: First half of the big game
parts.note: a large African beast hunted as big game, its full name cut to the first of two halves

explanation.walkthrough: The usual name for the beast is its full Greek name cut in half; the word is also British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form is the first part of the longer animal name, the big game beast itself.

clue.text: Cheat that's cornered by knight, initially

definitions.meaning: the chess piece that starts the game in a corner square, with a knight beside it

explanation.definitionFit: Means to swindle, and is also the castle in chess, set up in the corner next to the knight.

clue.text: Prepared to drive a Ford, finally in gear

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Ford

parts.note: in gear is dressed, gear being clothing

explanation.surface: A driver gets ready to drive a Ford once it is finally in gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Drive is the golf stroke: a golfer stands over the ball before driving it.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, to take up one's stance over the ball before hitting is this word.

clue.text: Food in repast is oddly deficient

indicators.note: oddly deficient says the odd-placed letters are missing, so the even ones remain

explanation.surface: The meal is strangely lacking in nourishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for grub or things to eat, a snack or meal.

clue.text: Needful and correct rules hard to follow

indicators.note: to follow means the hard letter comes after the rules

parts.note: the dos, as in dos and don'ts, are the rules for correct behaviour
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Necessary and proper regulations are hard to keep to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The needful' is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for money, as in being short of what is required to pay.

clue.text: Her co-star excited a lot of players

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of her co-star are rearranged

explanation.surface: Her fellow star thrilled many of the actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' suggests actors next to 'co-star', but these are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A large group of instrumental musicians performing together is a lot of players.

clue.text: They may be in minutes — minutes kept in binders

indicators.note: kept in means the minutes letter is held inside the binders word

parts.note: ties are things that bind

explanation.surface: Meeting records filed in ring binders note when things happened.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'minutes' are a meeting's record; the second is the unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Hours and dates of events are recorded in a meeting's written record.
